To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LAD antigems can be differentiated by immunohistochemistry using the novel substrate, cylindroma.

(a) LAD sera bind to a benign epithelial neoplasm (cylindroma) in two distinctive patterns; (b) these patterns correspond to the expression of known hemidesmosomal and anchoring fibril antigens, respectively; (c) the LAD sera bind multiple antigens, and these may be related to the expression of the antigens on the surface of the tumour clusters.
the linear IgA autoantibodies bind to multiple target antigens associated with the hemidesmosomes (anchoring filaments) and the anchoring (collagen VII) fibrils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the pathogenesis of LAD.
the characterization and classification of LAD.
the characterization of antigens involved in the pathogenesis of LAD and the identification of autoantibodies to these antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LAD autoantigens are complex, and that the antigens are not restricted to the epidermis.
LAD sera bind to multiple antigens in the epidermal and the dermal aspects of the basement membrane zone.
the antigens recognized in LAD may be multiple, but that the majority may be associated with hemidesmomes and anchoring filaments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LAD is an autoantibody disease directed to multiple target antigens in the basement membrane zone.
the LAD autoantigens are not a single antigen or a group of related proteins but rather a complex of antigens that may be associated with the hemidesmosomes or the anchoring fibril complex.
the LAD autoantigen(s) is a component of hemidesmosome and anchoring fibril complexes, and is not a component of the anchoring filament complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LAD sera bind to two different patterns of antigens in the basement membrane.
the antigens recognized by LAD sera are complex and may target multiple components of hemidesmomes and anchoring filaments.
we have shown that the LAD target antigents may be associated with the anchoring fibrillar components.
